## Start with criteria, not a prompt

Write the user, need, must-haves and restrictions first. Only then decide whether AI has a useful job. Good limited jobs include generating questions for an interview, listing alternative support strategies, explaining an unfamiliar term, or critiquing a draft checklist.

AI does not inspect the real stock, know the local machine rules, feel whether a fit works, or certify that a design is safe. A fluent answer may mix three categories:

| Category | Meaning | Student action |
|---|---|---|
| Fact | Checkable claim about the world | Verify with an authoritative source or measurement |
| Assumption | Unconfirmed condition treated as true | State it and test it |
| Suggestion | Possible direction or alternative | Compare against criteria |

## Bound the job

Instead of “design my tool holder,” ask: “Using only the measured values below, identify three support strategies and list the trade-offs. Do not choose dimensions or claim a load rating.” Never enter personal, confidential or identifying student information into an unapproved tool.

The human must select criteria, measure, test, decide, document and own the result.
